metaDesc: Six handpicked Phuket spa and wellness options, from multi-day detox and fitness retreats to good-value day spas for Thai and oil massage. Honest notes on what each place is known for and where it sits on the island.
ogTitle: Best Spa & Wellness in Phuket 2026 — 6 Picks
ogDesc: Phuket has spas ranging from walk-in shophouse massage to wellness resorts that sell packages in the thousands of dollars. So we split this list clearly into "retreats" you book for a multi-day program and "day spas" you drop into for a single treatment. All six places below are open and have recent reviews from 2025–2026. We checked location and what each is known for from real reviews and the venues' own pages rather than visiting in person. Choose based on whether you want a couple of relaxing hours or a longer reset.

blocks.html: Short answer: For a serious multi-day stay, pick a retreat like Phuket Cleanse or Atmanjai in Rawai, or Amatara at Cape Panwa for a luxury option. For a relaxing day massage, NARA in Chalong and Siladon in Patong are skilled and good value, while Oasis Spa in Kamala gives you a prettier full-spa setting.

items.name: Phuket Cleanse
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A fitness-and-detox retreat in Rawai on the island's south. The draw is an all-inclusive model that bundles accommodation, plant-based meals, bootcamp classes, Muay Thai, yoga and ice baths into one rate. It suits people who want to genuinely train and eat clean for several days, not just relax. Recent reviews rate it very highly for its friendly, community feel.

items.name: Atmanjai Wellness Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A beachfront detox center at Friendship Beach in Rawai, focused mainly on cleansing programs from juice cleanses up to its flagship Ultra Cleanse based on Dr. Bernard Jensen's protocols. Most programs require a minimum of three days. It fits people who want to reset their digestion and eating habits rather than just book a single massage.

items.name: Amatara Wellness Resort
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A five-star wellness resort on the hills of Cape Panwa with Andaman Sea views, a roughly 2,000-square-metre spa and a range of wellness programs covering detox, weight management, fitness and stress relief. It is the luxury, higher-spend option here, but you get private villas, healthy cuisine and a quiet setting well away from the tourist strips.

items.name: Oasis Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A day-spa brand with several branches in Thailand; in Phuket the standouts are Kamala (Turquoise Cove) and Laguna. The decor leans Mediterranean with private treatment villas, and the menu covers Thai and oil massage, hot stone, scrubs and multi-treatment packages. Free pickup is offered in some zones. Good for a prettier, full-service spa day.

items.name: NARA Massage & Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A day spa in the Chalong area that ranks among the most popular massage spots in that zone, with high review scores across a large number of reviews. The appeal is skilled hands at accessible prices, with Thai massage starting around 350 baht, plus foot, neck-and-shoulder and oil massage. Best for a good-quality, good-value massage without the luxury frills.

items.name: Siladon Spa
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A day spa in Patong inside The Marina Phuket Hotel, right in the tourist district and handy if you are staying around Patong. It offers popular multi-hour packages combining foot massage, body scrub, oil massage and a herbal compress, plus couples' rooms and family-friendly service. Reviews praise the experienced therapists and relaxed feel. A solid day-spa pick on the Patong side.

faq.q: Should I pick a wellness retreat or a day spa in Phuket?
faq.a: It depends on your time and goals. If you have several days and want a detox or fitness reset, go with a retreat like Phuket Cleanse, Atmanjai or Amatara, which sell multi-day programs. If you just want a relaxing massage during a holiday, a day spa like NARA, Siladon or Oasis is far cheaper and easier to book.

faq.q: How much does a Thai massage cost in Phuket?
faq.a: At a good day spa like NARA, Thai massage starts around 350 baht per hour. Multi-treatment packages at Siladon or Oasis cost more depending on what's included, and a resort spa like Amatara is considerably pricier. Always check current prices on the venue's page or a booking platform, as they change by season.

faq.q: What's the minimum stay for a detox retreat in Phuket?
faq.a: Most require around three days or more. Atmanjai, for example, starts every program at three days, and Phuket Cleanse allows flexible booking but is built around staying several days to see results. Amatara ranges from shorter packages to longer multi-day programs. Check the details and book ahead, as popular retreats fill quickly.
